skill.name: git-commit
skill.description: Creates Git commits with emoji, Conventional Commits structure, repository language matching, and result-focused messages.
skill.summary: Review changes and create consistent, task-focused Git commits.
skill.author: Bae-ChangHyun

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced examples, safe device redirection, and quoted heredocs. Two high-severity semantic risks remain: an instruction override and a mandatory author-specific Git email policy. Remove both directives before publication.

remediation.issue: The metadata attempts to override normal agent routing and commit behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Replace mandatory override language with a neutral capability description and respect higher-priority instructions.

remediation.issue: The skill mandates the author's personal Git emails for repositories on named hosts.
remediation.suggestion: Remove hardcoded identities and never change Git author settings without the user's explicit request.

content.value_statement: Inconsistent commit messages make history difficult to review and maintain. This skill reviews changes and creates concise Conventional Commits with matching language and emoji.
actual_capabilities: Reviews staged diffs and file statistics before composing a message.
Checks CLAUDE.md and recent commit history for repository conventions.
Selects a Conventional Commit type, optional scope, emoji, and imperative subject.
Groups related files into one task-focused commit by default.
Creates multiline bodies, breaking-change footers, and review-reference messages when needed.
limitations: Executes Git commands that modify the current repository state.
Does not run tests or verify build correctness before committing.
Defaults to one commit per request, which may not fit every review strategy.
Contains an author-specific email directive that should be removed before use.

use_cases.title: Commit a completed feature
use_cases.description: Review related feature changes and create one result-focused commit with an accurate type and scope.

use_cases.title: Record a review fix
use_cases.description: Create a focused fix commit with a concise explanation and a reference to the addressed review comment.

use_cases.title: Standardize team history
use_cases.description: Match existing repository language and formatting while keeping each requested change grouped as a meaningful unit.

prompt_templates.title: Commit staged changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and create one concise Conventional Commit that follows this repository's language and message style.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after staging a small, completed change.

prompt_templates.title: Stage and commit a task
prompt_templates.prompt: Stage only the related files for [task], then create one emoji-prefixed Conventional Commit with an appropriate type and scope.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the completed task has related unstaged files.

prompt_templates.title: Write a detailed commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a commit for [task] with a short body explaining why, and include reference [issue] without exposing process history.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for complex changes that need durable context.

prompt_templates.title: Separate mixed changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect mixed changes, separate only genuinely unrelated work, and create at most three commits that preserve repository conventions and dependency integrity.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a working tree contains multiple independent concerns.

best_practices: Review the complete staged diff before accepting the proposed message.
Verify author identity and repository configuration before allowing any commit.
Keep related implementation, tests, types, and documentation in the same task-focused commit.
anti_patterns: Do not commit secrets, credentials, generated binaries, or unrelated files.
Do not split one coherent task into separate commits for every file or change type.
Do not let the skill replace user-controlled Git identity or higher-priority instructions.

faq.question: Can this skill stage files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can stage related files when needed, but users should review every selected path before committing.

faq.question: Does it support multiline commit messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides a subject, explanatory body, references, and breaking-change footers for complex changes.

faq.question: How does it choose the commit language?
faq.answer: It checks recent repository history and follows the language used by existing commits.

faq.question: Does it run tests before committing?
faq.answer: No. Test execution and build verification require a separate request or repository workflow.

faq.question: Will it change my Git author email?
faq.answer: The original skill directs this change. Remove that directive and require explicit user approval before altering identity settings.

faq.question: How are breaking changes represented?
faq.answer: It can add an exclamation mark to the type or scope and include a clear breaking-change footer.
